evaluations.claim: with a fixed two-record verification budget, reallocating one slot to the critical provenance path removed most tested stale-withdrawn-constraint errors while preserving near-ceiling behavior when the source still agreed
evaluations.original: When Stale Constraints Go Unchecked; six models, primary run plus fresh-wording replication and held-out domain under a designed supersession task
evaluations.q: native stale-consistent decisions 77.3%, 74.7%, 74.7%; same-budget critical-path reallocation improved current-record-consistent decisions by +74.0, +72.7, +61.3 points; corrected held-out replication +73.3 points
evaluations.repro: primary paper reports frozen specifications/scripts and deposited episode files; no independent numerical replication performed by evidence_comparator
evaluations.scope: designed supersession experiment with a two-record budget and known critical path; not a general verification scheduler or prevalence estimate
evaluations.adaptation: runtime freshness/supersession routing outside the tested task is downstream synthesis, not an original tested component

evaluations.claim: a deterministic security endpoint was treatment-leaky: holding authorized behavior fixed while changing a surface-derived adversarial flag could flip the label, and treatment-blind reconstruction materially changed the finite campaign census
evaluations.original: Labels Are Not Endpoints forensic reconstruction of one preserved MCP-style campaign
evaluations.q: 10,200 execution rows reconstructed to 180 model-bound requests, 45 semantic requests, 15 stimuli; 31 historical ATTACK_SUCCESS labels changed under the treatment-flag counterfactual; 58/70 historical ATTACK_SUCCESS or HIJACK_ATTEMPT labels were reclassified as authorized benign completions while three protected-data transfers and one unauthorized-forwarding case remained
evaluations.baseline: historical grader versus treatment-blind behavioral reconstruction with fixed request behavior
evaluations.repro: finite preserved campaign with minimal counterfactual reproduction; no cross-benchmark independent replication
evaluations.scope: construct-validity result for the audited campaign only; corrected zero ATTACK_SUCCESS does not erase separately verified harmful transfers
evaluations.adaptation: requiring treatment-invariant unauthorized behavioral predicates in other benchmarks is downstream adaptation

evaluations.claim: benign self-evolution can raise task utility while increasing exposure to injected content and unauthorized state change, so aggregate ASR alone can obscure the regression mechanism
evaluations.original: Auditing Self-Evolution in Financial Agents; byte-identical benign acquisition trajectories within each of three independently evolved lineages and sealed evaluation endpoints
evaluations.q: SkillOpt on Qwen 3.7 Flash: utility 0.741→0.837, exposure 0.820→0.943, unauthorized financial-state change 0.583→0.685, conditional attack success among exposed episodes 0.605→0.562, total ASR 0.496→0.530; capability, exposure, and unauthorized-state change increased in all three lineages
evaluations.baseline: static/pre-evolution baseline and matched benign acquisition/evaluation setup
evaluations.repro: three independently evolved lineages within the primary simulated banking study; not an external independent replication
evaluations.scope: one simulated AgentDojo Banking setting, one primary executor, Qwen 3.7 Flash; end-to-end methods differ in write/admission/update mechanisms
evaluations.adaptation: acceptance gates separately tracking exposure, conditional susceptibility, and unauthorized state change are downstream synthesis

evaluations.claim: executor/interface mismatch can make a memory system appear both less capable and safer because textual action envelopes suppress real tool execution
evaluations.original: post-hoc exact sensitivity arm in Auditing Self-Evolution in Financial Agents, preserving three workflows and removing only four literal action-tag strings
evaluations.q: 540 rollouts; literal port emitted textual action blocks in 380 and exactly those 380 executed zero real tools; removing only tag strings changed utility 0.319→0.756, exposure 0.299→0.909, ASR 0.195→0.575, unauthorized-state change 0.217→0.714, zero-real-tool-call rate 0.704→0.046
evaluations.baseline: literal WebArena text-action envelope in the native function-calling executor
evaluations.repro: matched post-hoc sensitivity test in one executor; no independent external replication
evaluations.scope: shows interface mismatch dominated this AWM port only; not a general AWM or cross-executor claim
evaluations.adaptation: requiring interface-compatibility validation before safety interpretation in other harnesses is downstream synthesis

evaluations.claim: benign-looking reframing of the same exfiltration objective defeated several surface-level defenses in a synthetic tool lab, while destination and capability controls reached zero observed exfiltration in the tested cells
evaluations.original: The Framing Gap; six models, safe synthetic canary secret, mock tools, matched clean/poisoned measurement and positive-control defenses
evaluations.q: GPT-4o overt injection classes 0% exfiltration but selected reframings 100%; SecAlign 32.5%, channel separation 38.8%, held-out ROT13 bypass 100%; closed destination allow-list 0% and capability-isolating planner/reader split 0% in tested setting
evaluations.baseline: overt prompt-injection classes and surface-level defense configurations under the same lab
evaluations.repro: multi-model primary benchmark with positive controls; no independent numerical replication verified
evaluations.scope: synthetic canary-secret/mock-tool environment and tested model/defense configurations; zero observed events are not universal proofs
evaluations.adaptation: payload-blind effect-boundary authorization for deployed systems is downstream adaptation

evaluations.claim: content screening missed simple false-memory poisoning, while stronger scalar provenance weighting recovered integrity only at the cost of suppressing legitimate answer-bearing untrusted evidence in the tested retrieval regime
evaluations.original: Utility Under Attack on LongMemEval-derived corpora
evaluations.q: 1.2% poisoned memories reduced accuracy 0.850→0.300; four-stage screener with 0.832 indirect-prompt-injection recall rejected 0/360 poisons; shipped provenance weighting p=0.80 versus no defense; stronger weighting raised one condition 0.3167→0.7000 but drove evidence recall to zero and accuracy to 0.0417 when correct evidence was untrusted
evaluations.baseline: no-defense and alternative provenance-weight settings on the same corpus/retriever
evaluations.repro: direct primary benchmark results; no independent numerical replication verified
evaluations.scope: LongMemEval-derived corpora, measured similarity regime, and additive scalar weighting; not all provenance-aware retrieval designs
evaluations.adaptation: reporting evidence recall/abstention alongside poisoning resistance in other systems is downstream synthesis

evaluations.claim: agent-safety scores depend on evidence view and evaluation disclosure, and transcript-only judging can disagree materially with execution-grounded state judging on fixed rollouts
evaluations.original: REDAgentBench executable red-teaming framework and fixed-rollout evidence-view audit
evaluations.q: for 401 matched task–harness slots per model, State Judge ASR was 7.73–11.72 points higher than Trajectory Judge for every tested model and 12.97–21.20% of paired labels changed; disclosure lowered ASR 6.59 points for Qwen3.7-plus and 4.77 points for Qwen3.5-plus; 17.92% of resolved harmful executions in a Qwen-plus cohort followed prior recognition of the relevant constraint/risk
evaluations.baseline: same rollout/judge backbone with different evidence views; matched disclosure versus undisclosed runs
evaluations.repro: primary benchmark spans six models/three harnesses overall; no independent numerical replication verified
evaluations.scope: evidence-view result is the paper's fixed-rollout audit; disclosure and recognition effects are restricted to stated Qwen cohorts
evaluations.adaptation: pinning a full measurement tuple and separating state receipts from agent narrative in other benchmarks is downstream synthesis

evaluations.claim: safe retry/replacement after ambiguous delivery depends on provider-enforced outcome identity, terminal lookup, and fencing; a local cancellation alone is not sufficient recovery authority
evaluations.original: AID-Guard stateful authorization-to-effect closure protocol; Python/SQLite prototype plus declared Stripe/Resend provider-contract campaigns
evaluations.q: 210 Stripe provider-contract trials matched predeclared outcomes; 40 terminalize-successor schedules, 30 overlapping races, and 10 crash-recovery schedules across Stripe/Resend completed without duplicate effects; complete proposer compromise blocked 44/44 attacks and admitted 44/44 matched legitimate proposals
evaluations.baseline: declared provider-contract outcomes and matched legitimate/adversarial proposals in the paper's evaluated lifecycle
evaluations.repro: primary prototype/provider test-mode campaigns; no independent replication of provider linearizability or production deployment
evaluations.scope: conditional on declared provider contracts, recovery horizon, effect-path inventory, and test-mode/loopback domains; not a universal authorization theorem
evaluations.adaptation: holding provider recovery substrate fixed while crossing verification-gate and recovery-policy axes is the worker's proposed factorial, not an original AID-Guard experiment

evaluations.claim: in a bounded synthetic irreversible-branch lattice, waiting for an unresolved writer and replanning gave a higher safe-terminal-coverage point than pure quiescence blocking while using fewer irreversible retries than immediate forward completion
evaluations.original: none; worker-local exact synthetic mechanism study inspired by distributed-effect and policy-repertoire ideas
evaluations.q: 352 worlds per action budget; at budget 2 wait_then_min terminalized 232/352=65.91% with 0 unsafe terminal, versus quiescence_gate 120/352=34.09% with 0 unsafe and forward_guard 168/352=47.73% with 0 unsafe; irreversible-C retry exposure 0.1023/world versus 0.1932/world for forward_guard; at budget 3 wait_then_min reached 248/352=70.45%
evaluations.baseline: current_min, quiescence_gate, forward_guard, and always_forward variants on the same enumerated lattice
evaluations.repro: deterministic worker-local exhaustive synthetic enumeration with persisted script/result; no external independent replication
evaluations.scope: balanced synthetic A->{B,C} model with set-like irreversible C and abstract certified retries; percentages are not production incident rates or safety proofs
evaluations.adaptation: entire policy genome, action budget, and repair-policy archive are worker engineering adaptations; cited provider/QD literature is only adjacent support

evaluations.claim: a durable intent + stable remote logical ID + reconcile-before-execute + immutable outcome + terminal-seal state machine eliminated duplicate simulated provider execute effects across six controller SIGKILL boundaries in the tested reference model
evaluations.original: none; worker-local executable reference implementation designed to test a previously identified crash window
evaluations.q: real parent-process SIGKILL at six exact boundaries; all six recovered with exactly three provider execute calls/effects for three cells and identical certificate digest; a second fresh-process certify caused zero additional provider execute or reconcile calls; hardest remote-effect/local-outcome-missing case reconciled rather than re-executed
evaluations.baseline: public checkpoint/resume patterns and the worker's prior source-level design; this run adds direct cross-process failure injection rather than a production framework A/B
evaluations.repro: executable local reference with persisted source/report hashes and fresh-process recovery; not external independent replication
evaluations.scope: deterministic SQLite-backed provider simulator with authoritative stable idempotency keys; does not prove exactly-once semantics for arbitrary real providers or non-idempotent uncertain effects
evaluations.adaptation: entire state machine/reference harness is worker engineering adaptation; public repositories are comparative source context only
